title: Tin cans go to war
body:
The War Production Board ordered every American town of more than 25,000 people to start collecting tin cans.

Japan's conquests in Southeast Asia had cut off most of America's tin. Families peeled off labels, rinsed the cans, and stepped them flat.
photoNote: Harry Cardio, 10, of the Gramercy Boys' Club in New York tears off labels and flattens cans for the tin salvage drive, 1942. International News Photos, public domain.
